audited_source_corrections.action: Used finite-support functions from exponent beta into base alpha in both the synthetic construction and the exercise.
audited_source_corrections.source_issue_or_choice: The source defines finfun(alpha,beta) as finitely supported functions alpha to beta, then calls its order type alpha to the beta. Such functions instead represent beta to the alpha; the base and exponent arguments are reversed in both uses.
audited_source_corrections.chosen_treatment: தமிழ் கட்டமைப்பிலும் பயிற்சியிலும் அடுக்குக்குறியாகிய beta இலிருந்து அடியாகிய alpha க்கான முடிவுறு ஆதரவுச் சார்புகளைப் பயன்படுத்துகிறது.
audited_source_corrections.alternatives_considered: Changing the definition of finfun itself or retaining a construction whose zero-exponent and successor cases contradict the displayed recursion.
audited_source_corrections.rationale: finfun(0,alpha) contains the empty function and has order type 1; finfun(1,alpha) has order type alpha, as required by alpha^0=1 and alpha^1=alpha.
audited_source_corrections.precise_review_question: Do the synthetic construction and exercise both use finfun(beta,alpha) for alpha^beta?

audited_source_corrections.action: Excluded the zero exponent from the positive-limit union in the ordinal-exponentiation recursion.
audited_source_corrections.source_issue_or_choice: The source's limit union includes exponent 0 for every base. For base 0 and positive limit beta, the union includes 0^0=1 and yields 1, conflicting with the synthetic function order type and with 0 to every positive successor being 0.
audited_source_corrections.chosen_treatment: தமிழ் நேர்ம எல்லை அடுக்கில் பூச்சிய அடுக்கை மட்டும் விலக்கி 0 இன் நேர்ம அடுக்குகள் அனைத்தும் 0 ஆக இருப்பதைப் பாதுகாக்கிறது.
audited_source_corrections.alternatives_considered: Adding a separate zero-base case while retaining the original limit formula only under alpha>0; excluding base 0 from the chapter entirely.
audited_source_corrections.rationale: For every nonzero base, removing the initial exponent-0 value leaves the same limit supremum; for zero base it gives 0 at positive limits, agreeing with the corrected finite-support construction.
audited_source_corrections.precise_review_question: Does the limit clause agree with 0^beta=0 for every beta>0 while retaining ordinary nonzero-base exponentiation?
